target: leaf apex (PO:0020137) not spine-tipped (negation of FLOPO:0991210 spine-tipped); leaf itself present
fix: '<sub-part> absent' where the sub-part is a tip structure (terminal spine, mucro, awn, hair-point, apiculus) is an absence of that structure on the apex of the organ in the surrounding sentence, never an absence of the organ; if the sub-part has no PO term, drop the absence or negate the matching shape value class
reason: 'Terminal spine absent' describes the leaf tip of this moss; the leaves are present and imbricate

target: stem (PO:0009047) short (decreased length); no absence
fix: 'with X-less appearance', 'appearing X-less', 'seemingly/apparently X-less', 'subacaulescent' are statements of appearance; read as reduced size of X, never as X absent
reason: The flora says the stems are very short and the plant only looks stemless

target: geographic context: sporophytes (capsules) unknown in northern-hemisphere material; capsule colour comes from other material. Also the moss capsule bearer should be sporangium (PO:0025094), not capsule fruit (PO:0030091)
fix: 'absent in <region/collection> material', 'not known from <region>', 'unknown in X' are restrictions to a region or set of specimens; keep as a contextual statement, not a taxon-wide absence. In bryophyte floras map 'capsule' to sporangium (PO:0025094)
reason: The absence is limited to specimens from part of the range; elsewhere the capsule is described

target: no annotation (sporophytes not observed = unknown, not absent)
fix: 'not seen', 'not observed', 'unknown', 'not known', 'not available' express missing observation; never annotate them as absent. Remove 'sporophyte' as a synonym of whole plant (PO:0000003) for moss floras, where it names the sporangium-bearing generation
reason: 'Sporophytes not seen' says the material lacked sporophytes; it was mapped through the synonym sporophyte → whole plant

target: leaf (PO:0025034) non-deciduous (PATO:0001732), or no annotation
fix: 'without <quality-adjective> <part>' (without deciduous leaves, without decurrent leaves) negates the quality on the part, not the part; read as part + negated/opposite quality, never part absent
reason: The plant has leaves; the statement only says the distal leaves are not deciduous

target: stipel (PO:0020051) absent (PATO:0000462); stipule (PO:0020041) caducous stays
fix: Map 'stipelle(s)/stipel(s)/stipellae' to stipel PO:0020051 before any stem match on 'stip-'; 'stipelles absentes' / 'sans stipelles' / 'exstipellate' = stipel absent, never stipule absent
reason: Stipels (stipule-like structures at the leaflet base) are absent; stipules are present and caducous: different organs

target: 'sometimes absent' refers to a subset (most likely the outer female florets of the head); the heads have few to many flowers
fix: 'parfois absent(e)s', 'sometimes/occasionally/rarely absent' is variable presence; annotate as a variable or contextual statement (or not at all), never as a taxon-wide absence. Resolve the subject of an elliptic 'parfois absentes' from the preceding noun in the sentence
reason: Variable absence of some florets at genus level does not contradict flowers being present

target: stipel (PO:0020051) absent (PATO:0000462); stipule caducous stays
fix: Same as for 'stipelles absentes': 'sans stipelles' = stipel PO:0020051 absent, not stipule
reason: Stipels and stipules are different organs; the leaf is without stipels and has caducous stipules

target: genus-level variation: petals present and emarginate in most species, absent in a few (likely 'parfois/rarement absents' with the qualifier lost)
fix: In genus descriptions, a bare 'absents' next to a description of the same part is almost always 'rarely/sometimes absent'; when the sentence also describes the part, treat the absence as variable, not taxon-wide
reason: Petals of Ventilago are usually present (hooded, emarginate) and absent only in some species

target: variable presence: bracts (probably the bracteoles) sometimes absent; when present they are violet-yellow
fix: 'parfois absent(e)s' = variable presence; do not assert absent (PATO:0000462) taxon-wide
reason: Being sometimes absent does not contradict their colour when present

target: plumule (PO:0020032) absent (PATO:0000462); seed reticulate stays (testa)
fix: Map 'plumule' to PO:0020032 (an embryo part); a missing lexicon entry must not make the sentence fall back to its containing organ (seed). An absence whose subject is not in the lexicon is dropped, never moved up to the parent
reason: The plumule of the embryo is absent; the seed itself is present and reticulate

target: member/stage: flowers borne on leafless stems or branches (or at a leafless time); leaves present and coriaceous with age
fix: 'sur rameaux/tiges sans feuilles', 'sur le vieux bois sans feuilles', 'sans feuilles à la floraison' describe leafless shoots or a stage; annotate the shoot axis or the stage, not leaf absent for the taxon
reason: A climber with described coriaceous leaves is not leafless; 'sans feuilles' qualifies flowering stems or a stage

target: floret type: style absent in the sterile ray florets; disc florets have a style and a glabrous corolla tube
fix: In Asteraceae, statements in the ray-floret sentence ('style absent', 'stérile') are restricted to ray florets; annotate with the floret context and never as a taxon-wide absence
reason: Aspilia ray florets are neuter without a style; the disc florets have one

target: variable presence: petals sometimes absent, otherwise deeply bilobed
fix: 'parfois absents' = variable presence, not absent
reason: Petals that are sometimes missing are described when present

target: different bracts: external ostiolar bracts of the fig absent; the membranous bracts are other bracts (basal bracts or internal ostiolar bracts)
fix: '(ostiole) sans bractées externes' = external ostiolar bracts absent; only that bract set is absent. Without a PO term for ostiolar bracts, use bract with the ostiole context or drop the absence, never 'bract absent'
reason: Figs have several sets of bracts; only the outer ostiolar ones are absent

target: different bracts: external ostiolar bracts absent; persistent bases belong to the basal bracts (or stipules) of the fig
fix: As for 'sans bractées externes': an absence qualified by 'externes/internes/basales/de l'ostiole' applies only to that set of bracts
reason: The absence and the persistent bases are about different bracts

target: sex: stamens absent in female flowers; sessile stamens in male flowers (dioecious Garcinia)
fix: Statements in a 'fleurs femelles'/'fleurs mâles' sentence or block carry that sex as context; 'étamines absentes' in female flowers is never a taxon-wide absence
reason: Garcinia is dioecious; the male flowers have sessile stamens

target: involucral bract (PO:0009045) obtuse; the absence is about bracts on the scapes (scape without bracts)
fix: In Asteraceae the bracts described with apex shape in the head sentence are involucral bracts (phyllaries) → PO:0009045; '(hampes) dépourvues de bractées' is about the scape. Keep the two bract kinds apart
reason: The scapes have no bracts; the obtuse bracts are those of the involucre

target: position: leaves absent at the upper nodes only; the convex statement belongs to the leaf midvein (PO:0020139)
fix: 'absent(e)s aux nœuds supérieurs / à la base / sur les rameaux florifères' restricts absence to a position; annotate with that context, never as absence for the taxon. 'nervure médiane' maps to leaf midvein
reason: Leaves present lower on the stem; only the upper nodes lack them

target: member or age: one axis (e.g. young branchlets) without lenticels, another (older branches or trunk bark) with large lenticels
fix: 'non lenticellé(s)' attached to a named member (jeunes rameaux, rameaux) is restricted to that member; annotate as the member's quality, not as lenticel absent for the taxon
reason: Strychnos descriptions normally contrast young and older axes for lenticels

target: floret/fruit type: pappus absent on one kind of achene (ray or disc) and present (awns) on the other
fix: In Asteraceae, pappus statements in ray-achene vs disc-achene sentences carry the floret/fruit type as context; an opposite pappus statement in the same taxon signals two achene types, not a contradiction
reason: Synedrella has dimorphic achenes; the flora describes the pappus separately for each

target: sepal (PO:0009031) without visible veins (absence restricted to the vascular bundles of the sepal); 'nervures bouclées' = leaf veins looped/brochidodromous (not falciform)
fix: '<organ> non nervié(s)' / 'sans nervures' is about the veins of that organ only; bind the absence to the organ named (sepal), never to a generic vascular bundle shared with leaf-vein statements
reason: Absence of veins on the sepals and looped leaf veins are about different organs

target: member: the basal leaves (sheaths) lack a blade; the upper leaves have a dark green leaf lamina
fix: 'les basales/inférieures sans limbe' restricts the absence to the basal leaves; annotate as basal leaf + lamina absent, or drop, never leaf lamina absent for the taxon
reason: Sedges often have bladeless basal sheaths and bladed upper leaves

target: 'écailleuses' probably refers to the glumes or reduced leaf sheaths, not the inflorescence bracts; the involucral bracts are absent
fix: In Cyperaceae, 'écailles/écailleuses' in the spikelet sentence are glumes (spikelet bracts), separate from the inflorescence bracts; keep glumes from matching the same 'bract' as an involucral-bract absence
reason: Eleocharis lacks inflorescence bracts but has scale-like glumes

target: member: the lower leaves (sheaths) have no blade; the blades of the other leaves are glabrous ('sinon glabre')
fix: '(feuilles inférieures) sans limbe' is limited to those leaves; the 'sinon/otherwise' in the other statement confirms a contrast between members
reason: Lower bladeless sheaths and glabrous upper blades are both true

target: undetermined: the 'dépourvu de bractées' subject (inflorescence axis or pedicel?) and the 'largement ovées' subject (bracts or another organ?) cannot be resolved from the excerpts
fix: A masculine singular '(X) dépourvu de bractées' refers to a named axis (pédicelle, pédoncule, axe); resolve the head noun before annotating; without it, do not annotate a bract absence
reason: The excerpts are too short to tell which part each statement is about

target: member: branchlets (rameaux) without lenticels; the bark or older stem is lenticellate
fix: 'rameaux non lenticellés' is a quality of the branches (PO:0025073), not lenticel absent for the taxon; a 'lenticellé(e)' statement elsewhere about bark/trunk is a different member
reason: The two statements name different axes

target: intersecondary veins absent (no PO term: drop or use a FLOPO anatomy class); tertiary leaf vein (PO:0008021) percurrent
fix: Vein orders ('intersecondary', 'tertiary', 'quaternary', 'secondary') must map to their own vein class (PO:0020140, PO:0008021, ...) or be dropped; never fall back to the generic vascular bundle (PO:0005020), which makes the absence of one order contradict every other
reason: Only the intersecondary veins are absent; the tertiary veins are described

target: stage or member: flowering shoots, or the plant at flowering, without leaves; leaves present and slightly shining otherwise
fix: 'without leaves' inside an inflorescence/flowering-shoot or phenology sentence ('flowering when without leaves') is a stage or member context, not leaf absent for the taxon
reason: The leaves are described; the leafless statement is about a stage or flowering shoots

target: latex (no PO term; laticifer PO:0025031 is not the same thing) not white/absent from the bark slash; drop the bark absence. Bark granular stays
fix: 'without <exudate>' (latex, sap, resin, exudate, gum), especially with a colour ('without white latex'), is about the exudate, not about the organ it comes from; never map it to absence of that organ
reason: The bark is present and granular; the statement only says it has no white latex
